clue.text: First man to devise an outlet in wrought iron

indicators.note: the outlet sits inside the reworked letters of iron
wrought means worked or shaped, so the letters of iron are worked into a new order

parts.note: a vent is an outlet for air or gas

explanation.surface: A tale of whoever first fashioned a vent in a piece of wrought-iron work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrought' turns IRON into INOR, and 'in' puts VENT inside it, after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever is first to devise something is its originator, a creator of new things.

clue.text: Pressure is put on it to do evening work

definitions.text: Pressure is put on it to do evening work

parts.words: Pressure is put on it to do evening work
parts.note: evening reads as making even, smoothing creases, not night-time work, and the pressure is pressing down on cloth

explanation.surface: Someone is leaned on to do a night shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evening' is the act of making things even, not the hours after dusk: pressing clothes flat.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned smoothing tool pressed down on cloth to make it even.

clue.text: FBI agents housed in suitable fabrication

indicators.note: the agents are lodged inside the word for suitable, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: suitable means fit
G-men is slang for FBI agents (government men)

explanation.surface: FBI agents are given proper lodgings in some invented story.
explanation.definitionFit: A fabrication is an invention of the mind, something imagined and untrue.

clue.text: German-speaking city girl rising after six

indicators.note: the girl's piece comes after the six in the answer

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the girl's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl from a German-speaking city gets up after six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns ANNE into ENNA, which goes 'after' VI.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria's capital, where German is the main language spoken.

clue.text: Clucking female taking small brother in a place near Jerusalem

indicators.note: the hen takes in the brother, holding it inside her

parts.note: a hen is a female bird that clucks
bro is a short form of brother

explanation.surface: A clucking hen adopts a little brother somewhere near Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: A West Bank city south of Jerusalem, ancient and holy to several faiths.

clue.text: Last thing one would expect to get from an investment

definitions.text: Last thing one would expect to get from an investment

parts.words: Last thing one would expect to get from an investment
parts.note: last thing one would expect sounds like something unlikely, but it is literally the closing payment a shareholder receives

explanation.surface: Something no investor should hope for.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'last thing one would expect' means very unlikely; here it is literal, the closing payout of a company being wound up.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing payout to shareholders, often when a company winds up.

clue.text: A deed that doesn't make sense

definitions.text: A deed that doesn't make sense

parts.words: A deed that doesn't make sense
parts.note: a plain description of a senseless act, perhaps hinting at a legal deed

explanation.surface: A legal document that is nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A senseless act is a silly, unwise piece of behaviour.

clue.text: Establishment where pup pets are ill treated?

definitions.text: Establishment where pup pets are ill treated?

parts.words: Establishment where pup pets are ill treated?
parts.note: pup pets run together into puppets, and ill treated means the sick are treated, not abused

explanation.surface: A cruel kennel where young dogs are mistreated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pup pets' joins up as puppets, toys; 'ill treated' means the sick ones get care, not that they are abused.
explanation.definitionFit: A repair shop for broken toy figures, styled as an infirmary for playthings.

clue.text: Powerful biblical king dividing a trifling sum of money

indicators.note: the king splits the coin in two by sitting inside it

parts.note: a cent is a coin of very small value
Og was King of Bashan in the Bible

explanation.surface: A mighty biblical monarch splitting a few pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: A cogent argument is compelling and forceful, so strong in persuasion.

clue.text: A fellow training a baboon from West Africa

parts.note: a fellow is a man
drill is training, as in military exercises

explanation.surface: A man is teaching tricks to an African primate.
explanation.definitionFit: A large brightly faced primate of West African forests, related to the drill.

clue.text: Hot resentment that is inwardly right

indicators.note: inwardly says the letter for right goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Seething anger that feels justified deep down.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger or wrath, a burning sense of grievance.

clue.text: Immediate consequence a fall

parts.note: a fall suggests a tumble, but it is the American name for autumn, and the season after it follows directly

explanation.surface: What happens straight after someone takes a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a fall' looks like a tumble; it is autumn, the American word, and the cold season comes straight after.
explanation.definitionFit: The cold season comes directly after autumn in the calendar.

clue.text: One Scottish loch located in another neighbourhood

indicators.note: one loch is placed within the other, so one word sits inside the second

parts.note: Loch Ness is another, more famous Scottish loch
Loch Earn is a loch in Perthshire, Scotland

explanation.surface: One Scottish loch found in the vicinity of another.
explanation.walkthrough: Loch Earn and Loch Ness are both in Scotland; EARN goes inside NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being near or close by; proximity, the sense of the vicinity.

clue.text: Knock up a good score at golf

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: par is the standard score for a golf hole

explanation.surface: Notching a decent golf round.
explanation.definitionFit: A rap is a sharp tap or blow, as on a door.

clue.text: Taking part in a property deal

definitions.meaning: holding a stake in property jointly with someone, as in time-share or shared ownership

explanation.definitionFit: Participating means joining in, and joint ownership deals split a home between buyers.

clue.text: Unhealthy little state in Central America!

definitions.meaning: .... is a short form of Illinois, a state in the middle of the USA, not in the region usually called Central America

explanation.definitionFit: Sick means poorly; and Illinois is a Midwestern US state with a short form of three letters.

clue.text: Uncle's little store of champagne?

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker, and pop is both fizzy wine and slang for pawning goods

explanation.surface: A relative keeps a small cellar of fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'uncle' is a pawnbroker and to 'pop' something is to pawn it; pop is also fizzy drink, hence the champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: Old British slang for a pawnbroker's premises, where goods are pawned.

clue.text: A key figure in the services

definitions.text: A key figure in the services

parts.words: A key figure in the services
parts.note: key suggests importance and services the armed forces, but keys are on a keyboard instrument and services are church worship

explanation.surface: An important person in the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' and 'services' suggest military rank; the keys are on an instrument and the services are church worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A church musician who plays the keyboard instrument at worship.

clue.text: Quickly burns up the miles?

parts.note: burns up the miles is to travel very fast, and the verb also means singes

explanation.surface: A driver racing along the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To singe is to burn, and in slang to drive at high speed is to tear along.

clue.text: Work in the dark to get negative results

definitions.text: Work in the dark to get negative results

parts.words: Work in the dark to get negative results
parts.note: sounds like failing blindly, but describes treating film in a darkroom to bring out negatives

explanation.surface: Someone labouring without information and failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negative results' suggests failure; in photography film is treated in a darkroom to produce negatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers process exposed film chemically in a darkroom.

clue.text: It means raising the subject at the palace

definitions.text: It means raising the subject at the palace

parts.words: It means raising the subject at the palace
parts.note: raising the subject sounds like bringing up a topic, but a subject of the monarch is raised to knighthood

explanation.surface: Bringing up a topic during a royal visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising the subject' is mentioning a topic; here a royal subject is elevated by the sword touch at a knighting ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial tap with a sword that confers knighthood, now any honour.

clue.text: They have news or review it

indicators.note: to re-view is to look again, so the letters of news or are seen in a new order

explanation.surface: People who own news or review publications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review' turns NEWS OR into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Proprietors possess things, so they are the people who have them.

clue.text: Vaulted church in a revolutionary ambience

indicators.note: an ambience is a surrounding setting, so the church is surrounded by the other letters

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary, a communist

explanation.surface: A domed church with a radical atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaulted ceilings are curved over like a bow.

clue.text: Associations formed by our GPs

indicators.note: the answer is made up from these letters, reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Medical partnerships set up by local family doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formed by' rearranges OUR GPS. GPs are family doctors in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Associations are bodies of people banded together, clubs or bands.

clue.text: A Roman quartet retracing a Roman road

indicators.note: retracing means going back over the path, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four Romans walk back along a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retracing' turns A IV round to the answer; 'a Roman road' is the definition, since via is Latin for road.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for road or way, as in the Appian Way.

clue.text: The top hostel in a ramshackle place, apparently

indicators.note: the hostel goes inside the rearranged letters
ramshackle means tumbledown, so the letters of place are knocked about

parts.note: an inn is a hostelry

explanation.surface: The best lodging is apparently in a rundown spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ramshackle' makes PACLE of PLACE, and 'in' puts INN after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit or peak, the highest point of something.

clue.text: Little distinction?

parts.note: little distinction suggests a small honour, but means a fine, subtle difference

explanation.surface: A minor honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtlety, a fine point of difference that is hard to see.

clue.text: The unflappability one would need to take over the leadership of the Liberal party

definitions.text: The unflappability one would need to take over the leadership of the Liberal party

parts.words: The unflappability one would need to take over the leadership of the Liberal party
parts.note: a cool temperament is needed to lead, and David Steel led the British Liberal Party from 1976 to 1988

explanation.surface: Calm required to become head of a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: David Steel was leader of Britain's Liberal Party (1976 to 1988): taking over from him needs the iron calm, with his name in the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Composure under pressure, a cool, unshakeable temperament.
